summary: Tree recursion plus BST structure. Most answers come from a recursion that returns something upward (height, sum, subtree info); BSTs add the key fact that an inorder traversal is sorted. Special tools here: Morris traversal for O(1) space, BFS with a horizontal-distance key for top/vertical views, and the two-bounds trick for BST validity and LCA.

thoughtProcess.title: Decide what each recursive call RETURNS, then compose the parent's answer.
thoughtProcess.body: Height returns 1+max(childHeights); diameter tracks the best left+right while returning height; sum returns node+left+right. Nail the return contract first.

thoughtProcess.title: BST? Inorder is sorted — lean on it.
thoughtProcess.body: Kth-smallest = kth inorder node; validate/recover BST by checking the inorder is increasing; range and search prune by comparing to node.val.

thoughtProcess.title: Views (top/vertical) = BFS carrying a horizontal distance (hd).
thoughtProcess.body: Root hd=0, left child hd-1, right hd+1. Group nodes by hd; top view keeps the first node seen per hd, vertical order keeps all (top to bottom).

keyPatterns.name: Return-value recursion
keyPatterns.template: int h(node){ if(!node) return 0; int L=h(node.left),R=h(node.right); best=max(best,L+R); return 1+max(L,R);}

keyPatterns.name: BST inorder
keyPatterns.when: Kth smallest, validate, recover, common nodes
keyPatterns.template: inorder(node): inorder(left); visit(node); inorder(right)  // yields sorted order

keyPatterns.name: LCA by node values / bounds
keyPatterns.template:
BST: walk down, go left if both < node, right if both > node, else current is LCA.
General tree: recurse; node where left and right both find a target is the LCA.

keyPatterns.name: BFS with horizontal distance
keyPatterns.template: queue of (node,hd); map hd->nodes; root hd=0, left hd-1, right hd+1

keyPatterns.name: Morris traversal
keyPatterns.when: Inorder in O(1) extra space (no stack/recursion)
keyPatterns.template: thread each node's inorder predecessor to it; unthread on the second visit

commonMistakes.title: BST validity checked against parent only, not ancestors
commonMistakes.right: boolean valid(node,long lo,long hi){ if(node==null)return true; if(node.val<=lo||node.val>=hi)return false; ... }
commonMistakes.why: A node must respect ALL ancestor bounds, not just its immediate children; carry (lo,hi) down and use long to dodge Integer.MIN/MAX edge values.

commonMistakes.title: Morris traversal that never removes the thread
commonMistakes.right: on revisiting a threaded predecessor, set pred.right=null before visiting
commonMistakes.why: Leaving threads in place corrupts the tree into a cycle; you must unthread on the second encounter.

edgeCases: Empty tree (root == null) and single node — base cases for every recursion.
Skewed tree (all-left or all-right) makes recursion depth O(N) — deep trees risk stack overflow.
BST bounds: a node holding Integer.MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE fails int-range checks — use long sentinels.
LCA where one node is an ancestor of the other, or a node isn't present — define the expected behaviour.
